questions.question: Describe about Earthquake risk factors
questions.solution_html:
• Earthquake Risk Factors
  • Population Density – More people in an area means more damage and deaths.
  • Building Quality – Weak or old buildings collapse easily during earthquakes.
  • Emergency Preparedness – Good rescue systems and public awareness reduce loss of life.
  • Tectonic Activity – Places near fault zones are more likely to experience earthquakes.
  • Ground Conditions – Soft soil can increase shaking and cause liquefaction.
  • Secondary Hazards – Earthquakes can also cause landslides, tsunamis, fires, floods, and aftershocks.
questions.final_answer: Secondary Hazards – Earthquakes can also cause landslides, tsunamis, fires, floods, and aftershocks

questions.question: Describe the health risks associated with animals to human
questions.solution_html:
• Health risks associated with animals to human
  • Spread of diseases – Animals can spread diseases like rabies and bird flu to humans through bites
  • food, water, or contact.
  • Allergies and breathing problems – Animal fur, feathers, and waste can cause allergies and asthma.
  • Injuries and poisoning – Some animals may bite, sting, or inject venom, causing injury or sickness.
questions.final_answer: Injuries and poisoning – Some animals may bite, sting, or inject venom, causing injury or sickness

questions.question: Discuss the role of dams and levees in mitigating flood risks through engineering solutions.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of dams and levees in mitigating flood risks through engineering solutions
  • Dams hold extra water and release it slowly to reduce floods.
  • Levees are walls or embankments along rivers that stop water from overflowing.
  • Both help protect people, houses, and land from flood damage.
questions.final_answer: Both help protect people, houses, and land from flood damage

questions.question: Explain the process of cyclone formation, focusing on the role of warm air, / moisture, and the Coriolis Effect.
questions.solution_html:
• Cyclones form over warm oceans where the air becomes warm and moist.
  • The warm air rises, creating a low-pressure area, and more air moves in.
  • As the air rises, it cools and condenses, forming clouds and releasing heat, which makes the system
  • stronger.
  • The Coriolis Effect (due to Earth’s rotation) causes the winds to spin around the low-pressure centre
  • forming a cyclone.
questions.final_answer: forming a cyclone
